subject: Chemistry
description: Atom components, isotopes, electronic configuration, periodic table

questions.stem: The atom contains which three FUNDAMENTAL particles?
questions.explanation: Proton (p, +1, in nucleus). Neutron (n, 0, in nucleus). Electron (e⁻, -1, in orbitals). Hydrogen nucleus has no neutron — just a proton. Quarks are sub-nucleon constituents (not 'fundamental atomic' in introductory chem).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: ISOTOPES are atoms of the same element that differ in:

options.option_text: Number of electrons in the neutral atom

questions.explanation: Isotopes — same Z (protons, same element), different A (mass number, different neutrons). Example: ¹²C (6 protons + 6 neutrons) vs ¹⁴C (6 protons + 8 neutrons). ¹⁴C is radioactive and used in carbon dating. All 3 H isotopes: ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium, radioactive).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The MODERN periodic table is arranged by:
questions.explanation: Moseley (1913) — atomic number (Z) is the fundamental basis. Mendeleev's original (1869) ordering by atomic mass had inconsistencies (Te-I, Ar-K, Co-Ni swaps). Moving to atomic number fixed these. Modern table: 7 periods, 18 groups (s, p, d, f blocks).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: An atom of CARBON has how many valence electrons?
questions.explanation: Carbon (Z=6): 1s² 2s² 2p². 2s² + 2p² = 4 valence electrons in outer shell → tetravalent. Forms 4 covalent bonds — basis of all of organic chemistry. Diamond (sp³), graphite (sp²), benzene, methane.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: RUTHERFORD's α-particle scattering experiment led to the discovery of the:
questions.explanation: Rutherford (1911) — fired α-particles at gold foil; a small fraction deflected sharply → concluded positive charge and mass are concentrated in a tiny nucleus. JJ Thomson — electron (1897, cathode rays). James Chadwick — neutron (1932).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which element has the atomic number 1?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen (H): Z=1, simplest and most abundant element in the universe (~75% by mass). He: Z=2. Li: Z=3. C: Z=6. N: Z=7. O: Z=8. First 20 is a basic recall: H He Li Be B C N O F Ne Na Mg Al Si P S Cl Ar K Ca.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: A CHEMICAL BOND formed by sharing of electrons between atoms is called:
questions.explanation: Covalent — electrons shared (H₂, O₂, CH₄, H₂O). Ionic — complete electron transfer (NaCl, MgO). Metallic — 'sea of delocalised electrons' in metals. Hydrogen bond — weak attraction between H (bonded to F/O/N) and lone pair of F/O/N on another molecule.
